{{Short description|Swedish statistician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2025}}

'''Lars Lyberg''' (1 December 1944&nbsp;– 9 March 2021)<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Trewin |first=Dennis |author-link=Dennis Trewin |date=23 August 2021 |title=Lars Lyberg, (1944–2021) |url=https://academic.oup.com/jrsssa/article/184/4/1606/7068841 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A: Statistics in Society |volume=184 |issue=4 |pages=1606–1607 |doi=10.1111/rssa.12694|url-access=subscription }}</ref> was a Swedish statistician, head of [[research and development]] at [[Statistics Sweden]], the founding editor of the ''[[Journal of Official Statistics]]'', and a Fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] and [[American Statistical Association]]. His research focused on [[data quality]], [[total survey error]], and research in the multinational, multiregional, and multicultural contexts.

== Education and career ==
Lyberg received his PhD in statistics from the [[Stockholm University]] where he also taught in 2003–2009 and 2010–2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Trewin |first1=Dennis |author-link1=Dennis Trewin |last2=Biemer |first2=Paul |last3=Groves |first3=Bob |author-link3=Robert Groves |title=Lars Lyberg Obituary |url=https://www.scb.se/contentassets/0727488185134f809290fd74e451e030/in-memory-of-lars-lyberg-founder-of-jos.pdf |access-date=17 April 2024 |website=[[Statistics Sweden]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=22 March 2021 |title=In memory of our colleague Professor Lars Lyberg (1944-12-01 – 2021-03-01) – Department of Statistics |url=https://www.su.se/cmlink/stockholms-universitet-samh%C3%A4llsvetenskapliga-fakulteten/statistiska-institutionen-nod/department-of-statistics/about-us-old/news/in-memory-of-our-colleague-professor-lars-lyberg-1944-12-01-2021-03-01-1.547470 |access-date=16 April 2024 |website=[[Stockholm University]]}}</ref>

He began his career at [[Statistics Sweden]] in 1966 and later directed its research and development department until his retirement in 2010. During his tenure, he represented Sweden in the development of [[International Organization for Standardization|ISO Standard]] 20252 on Market, Opinion and Social Research.<ref name=":0" />

In 1985, he founded the Journal of Official Statistics and served as editor-in-chief for 25 years.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Biemer |first=Paul |date=1 June 2022 |title=In Memory of Dr. Lars Lyberg Remembering a Giant in Survey Research 1944–2021 |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.2478/jos-2022-0018 |journal=[[Journal of Official Statistics]] |language=en |volume=38 |issue=2 |pages=353–366 |doi=10.2478/jos-2022-0018 |issn=2001-7367}}</ref>

He published numerous articles, books, conference volumes, and task force reports, most notably: ''Total Survey Error: Past, Present, and Future,''<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Groves |first1=Robert |last2=Lyberg |first2=Lars |author-link2=Lars Lyberg |year=2010 |title=Total Survey Error: Past, Present, and Future |url=https://academic.oup.com/poq/article/74/5/849/1817502 |journal=[[Public Opinion Quarterly]] |volume=74 |issue=5 |pages=849–879|doi=10.1093/poq/nfq065 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> ''Telephone Survey Methodology'',<ref>{{Cite book |title=Telephone Survey Methodology |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |year=1988 |isbn=978-0-471-20956-0}}</ref> ''Measurement Errors in Surveys'',<ref>{{Cite book |title=Measurement Errors in Surveys |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |year=1991 |isbn=978-1-118-15037-5}}</ref> ''Survey Measurement and Process Quality'',<ref>{{Cite book |title=Survey Measurement and Process Quality |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |isbn=978-1-118-49006-8}}</ref> ''Introduction to Survey Quality'',<ref>{{Cite book |title=Introduction to Survey Quality |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |year=2003 |isbn=978-0-471-45872-2}}</ref> ''Survey Methods in Multicultural, Multinational, and Multiregional Contexts'',<ref>{{Cite book |title=Survey Methods in Multinational, Multiregional, and Multicultural Contexts |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |year=2010 |isbn=978-0-470-60991-0}}</ref> ''Survey Error in Practice,''<ref>{{Cite book |title=Total Survey Error in Practice |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |year=2017 |isbn=978-1-119-04169-6}}</ref> ''AAPOR/WAPOR Task Force Report on Comparative Surveys'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=AAPOR/WAPOR Task Force Report on Quality in Comparative Surveys |url=https://aapor.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AAPOR-WAPOR-Task-Force-Report-on-Quality-in-Comparative-Surveys_Full-Report.pdf |access-date=29 August 2023 |website=AAPOR Reports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=AAPOR/WAPOR Task Force Report on Quality in Comparative Surveys |url=https://wapor.org/resources/aapor-wapor-task-force-report-on-quality-in-comparative-surveys/ |access-date=29 August 2023 |website=World Association for Public Opinion Research}}</ref> ''and Big Data Meets Survey Science,''<ref>{{Cite book |title=Big Data Meets Survey Science |publisher=[[Wiley Publishing]] |year=2020 |isbn=978-1-118-97632-6}}</ref> and posthumously the ''Handbook of Computational Social Science''<ref>{{Cite book |title=Handbook of Computational Social Science, Volume 1: Theory, Case Studies and == Personal life ==
He was married to Lilli Japec, a senior statistician at Statistics Sweden, and had two adopted sons from his first marriage.<ref name=":0" />

Known by his nickname "Lasse", he enjoyed American baseball, Southern cuisine, and vacationing in Florida.<ref name=":1" /> He was also a [[Association football|football (soccer)]] fan and coach.<ref name=":66">{{Cite journal |last=Lynn |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Lynn (statistician) |date=2022 |title=Acknowledgements |url=https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/798e3ef9-fe65-11ec-b94a-01aa75ed71a1/language-en|journal=Improving the measurement of poverty and social exclusion in Europe: reducing non-sampling errors|volume=2022 |pages=3 }}</ref> At the 20th anniversary of the Journal of Official Statistics, [[Edith de Leeuw]] and approximately 50 statisticians presented him with a spoof titled the "Journal of Obnoxious Statistics (JOBS)".<ref>{{Cite web |last=de Leeuw |first=Edith |author-link=Edith de Leeuw |title=JOBS |url=https://edithl.home.xs4all.nl/jobs.htm |access-date=17 April 2024 |website=edithl.home.xs4all.nl}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
Lyberg was an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] and a Fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1993, he was elected as a [[List of fellows of the American Statistical Association|Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ASA Fellows |url=https://ww2.amstat.org/fellows/ |access-date=9 February 2024 |website=American Statistical Association}}</ref>

In 2012, the International Association of Survey Statisticians (IASS) recognized him with the Waksberg Award for his contributions in the area of survey quality.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Waksberg Award {{!}} International Association of Survey Statisticians (IASS) |url=http://isi-iass.org/home/waksberg-award/ |access-date=17 April 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2013, he was awarded the [[Helen Dinerman]] Award from the [[World Association for Public Opinion Research|World Association for Public Research]]. The [[American Association for Public Opinion Research]] honored him in 2018 with the Award for Exceptionally Distinguished Achievement.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=18 October 2018 |title=AAPOR Award for Exceptionally Distinguished Achievement |url=https://academic.oup.com/poq/article-abstract/82/3/622/5136083 |journal=[[Public Opinion Quarterly]] |volume=82 |issue=3 |pages=622 |doi=10.1093/poq/nfy031|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In recognition of his achievements in statistics for societal benefit, the Swedish Statistical Association named him 2019 statistician of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Survey Statistician: IASS Newsletter |url=http://isi-iass.org/home/wp-content/uploads/Survey_Statistician_2021_July_N84_01.pdf |access-date=17 April 2024 |website=International Association of Survey Statisticians}}</ref>

A virtual memorial was held at the 2021 [[Joint Statistical Meetings|Joint Statistical Meeting]] where Lyberg was remembered for his scholarship, humility, and sense of humor.<ref name=":1" /> Since 2021, Demoskop has held The Lyberg Conference annually in Sweden with a YouTube live stream, covering topics concerning data collection, quality, and innovations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Lyberg conference |url=https://demoskop.se/en/the-lyberg-conference/ |access-date=17 April 2024 |website=Demoskop |language=en-GB}}</ref>
